title: fix(app-shell): a CEL comprehension macro's iteration variable is bound inside its macro, not flagged as out of scope (objectui#10538)
body:
Fixes #10538

Clause-②: no

Implemented by a dispatched dev run of the `domain:ui` seat 5, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01KUxVUa7e39aNjhkKi1gsoy`.

## What changes

`findUnknownRefs` in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-ref-check.ts` read every root identifier in a CEL source as a flow variable reference. So a comprehension macro's own iteration variable (`r` in `rows.map(r, r.subject)`) drew the amber "not in scope" warning. That included the assignment-value example in `@objectstack/spec`, `joinNonEmpty(rows.map(r, r.subject), "\n")`, in the `AssignmentValue` JSDoc.

`rootIdentifiers` now collects the bindings of `map`, `filter`, `exists`, `all` and `exists_one`, through a new private helper `macroBindings` in the same file. For a member call `.MACRO(v, ...)` whose first argument is a bare identifier, `v` is bound between that call's `(` and its matching `)`, and nowhere else. Scope is lexical: the receiver, and the same name after the closing `)`, are still roots. A nested macro binds each variable in its own span. `findUnknownRefs` itself is unchanged. The warning stays advisory; nothing about what blocks Save changes.

## Why the local scanner and not the parser-backed reader (H2, measured)

`@objectstack/formula` 17.4.0, already an app-shell dependency, exports `collectCelRootIdentifiers`. Measured on the five macros, it reports the bound variable too:

| source | `collectCelRootIdentifiers(source).roots` |
|---|---|
| `rows.map(r, r.subject)` | `["rows","r"]` |
| `rows.filter(x, x.done).size()` | `["rows","x"]` |
| `rows.exists(e, e.a > 1)` | `["rows","e"]` |
| `rows.all(a, a.ok)` | `["rows","a"]` |
| `rows.exists_one(o, o.id == 1)` | `["rows","o"]` |
| `rows.map(r, r.items.filter(i, i.ok))` | `["rows","r","i"]` |

Switching `findUnknownRefs` to that reader would keep this defect. So the fix stays in the local regex scanner, scoped to each macro's argument span, and no parser-backed path is added. The upstream walker has the same defect and its consumers inherit it. That is reported to the dispatching seat as a separate finding (see Acceptance notes). objectstack is not edited here.

## Pins

A new `describe` in `flow-ref-check.test.ts`, "findUnknownRefs (CEL comprehension macros bind their iteration variable) (objectui#10538)":

- the canonical example reports `[]`;
- each of the five macros (plus the three-argument `map`) with its own bound variable reports `[]`;
- a nested macro reports `[]`;
- negative legs: `rows.map(r, r.subject) + r` flags the trailing `r`; an inner variable used after its own macro closes is flagged; a bound variable used as a different macro's receiver is flagged; `rowz.map(r, r.subject)` flags `rowz` with suggestion `rows`; a member call that is not one of the five (`rows.join(sep, other)`) binds nothing.

Base vs fix, single file (`pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-ref-check.test.ts`, through the shared verify lock):

- base source, byte-identical to `21d34d5` (`git diff --quiet` exit 0), new pins added: exit 1, `Tests 6 failed | 15 passed (21)`. The canonical pin fails with `expected [ { token: 'r', …(1) } ] to deeply equal []`.
- with the fix (commit `5225195`): exit 0, `Tests 21 passed (21)`.

Two of the negative legs pass on the base as well; they guard against the fix binding too much.

## Gates (at head `9fd5fcc`, after merging `origin/main` `adeecd6`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/flow-expr-problems.test.ts`: exit 0, `Test Files 98 passed (98)`, `Tests 1357 passed | 1 skipped (1358)`. The skip is an existing spec-version `skipIf` in `flow-node-config.spec-reconciliation.test.ts`. The previews test is added because `flow-expr-problems.ts` is the one caller of `findUnknownRefs` outside the inspectors folder.
- `pnpm turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/app-shell --concurrency=2`: exit 0, `Tasks: 30 successful, 30 total`. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists `flow-ref-check.test.ts`, so the pins are type-checked.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the two changed source files: exit 0, no output.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `changeset:check`, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` and `node scripts/check-changeset-overwrite.mjs`: all exit 0.

Changeset: `.changeset/10538-cel-macro-bound-variable.md`, `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`.

## Acceptance notes

- Upstream, not filed by this PR (reported to the seat): `collectCelRootIdentifiers` in `@objectstack/formula` reports a macro-bound variable as a root, so its closed-root consumers refuse valid CEL. Probe on `@objectstack/lint` 17.4.0: `validateApprovalApprovers` on an approval node whose `expression` approver is `vars.list.map(x, x.id)` gives error `approval-expression-invalid`, "expression approver references `x`". The control `vars.list` gives no such error.
- `cel.bind(x, rows, x.size())` evaluates upstream (`ExpressionEngine.evaluate` gives `{ ok: true, value: 3 }`), and this scanner flags `cel` and `x` on it, before and after this change. `cel.bind` is outside the five macros this card rules on, and its shape differs: the variable is bound in the third argument only, and the receiver `cel` is a namespace constant. So it is reported to the seat, not changed here.
- Docs: no page under `content/docs` describes this designer warning, so there is no docs change.
